While studying classical piano, I briefly learned in music theory class about basso continuo, which is baroque-era improv over a bassline. That was fun, but I only really learned about chord progressions after I started playing jazz tunes out of a Real Book.
Kids who learned these skills would be more likely to keep them up later in life, rather than abandoning their instruments as soon as their parents stop schlepping them to music lessons.

Musical training should put more emphasis on teaching chord changes and how to play over them instead of the motor skill of memorizing classical pieces. These skills are usually only taught with jazz, but they're useful for all genres.
